verdicts.verify_by: run the shapes probe: `map ok: false has: false`; read values.go:1339-1352 for the copy cases
verdicts.tldr: a stored map gets no identity although every holder shares one *MapValue, and the documented reason for excluding it (a by-value copy) does not apply to maps
verdicts.details: ownObject handles only PointerValue, *FuncValue and *BoundMethodValue, so a *MapValue falls to `return nil`. TypedValue.Copy deep-copies only BigintValue, *ArrayValue and *StructValue and unrefCopy only arrays and structs; a map hits `default: cp = tv`, so it is a reference exactly like the func values the comment admits. reflect.gno:106 and reflect.go:55 group map with struct and array as 'may be ... a copy', which is false for maps. Fix: either add a `case *gno.MapValue` arm alongside FuncValue, or reword the exclusion so it names the real reason maps are left out.

verdicts.verify_by: read misc.go:222, realm.go:74-76, ownership.go:45-48, reflect.gno:60 | go test snippet comparing AddressFromPreimage("objectid:"+oid.String()) against DeriveObjectCryptoAddr(oid)
verdicts.tldr: hashing the id that Object.ID() returns, as the docs suggest, does not give the chain's address, and the consensus preimage depends on a debug Stringer
verdicts.details: The preimage uses PkgID.String(), which is `fmt.Sprintf("RID%X", pid.Hashlet[:])` (realm.go:74-75), uppercase with an RID prefix. X_objectInfo returns oid.String() as the id, and ObjectID.String() is MarshalAmino, `hex.EncodeToString(oid.PkgID.Hashlet[:])` lowercase with no prefix (ownership.go:47-48, 69-71). reflect.gno:60 documents addr as 'bech32, derived from id', so an indexer hashing `objectid:`+ID() gets a different address. Shared with #6139. Fix: build the preimage from the hashlet bytes or from oid.MarshalAmino rather than a fmt Stringer, or document the exact spelling.

verdicts.verify_by: filetest with persisted tok and Method; print reflect.Of(tok.Method) ok and HasIdentity before and after a crossing call; expect 'ok: false has: true' both times
verdicts.tldr: a realm following the docs on `tok.Method` waits for an address that never comes, because each evaluation is a fresh unstamped object that reports HasIdentity true
verdicts.details: Each evaluation of a method selector allocates a new `&BoundMethodValue{...}` and stamps only its PkgID (values.go:2253-2260), so NewTime stays 0, X_objectInfo takes the `!oid.IsFinalized()` branch and returns ok=false, hasIdentity=true. Asking again after the boundary evaluates tok.Method again and gets another fresh value, so the 'ask again after the call returns' answer in reflect.gno:70-74 never resolves. The method-expression half ((*Token).Method) was not traced. Fix: report HasIdentity false for a BoundMethodValue that is not persisted, or document that a method value only gets an identity once it is stored.
verdicts.evidence: values.go:2253-2260 `alloc.AllocateBoundMethod(); bmv := &BoundMethodValue{Func: mv, Receiver: rtv}; ... alloc.stampPkgID(&bmv.ObjectInfo, nil)`; reflect.go:26-31 returns `"", "", "", "", false, true` when !IsFinalized; ownership.go:107-108 IsFinalized is `oid.NewTime != 0`

verdicts.verify_by: Benchmark X_objectInfo on a stamped object with DeclaredType Name of 8 B, 1 KB, 64 KB, 1 MB; compare with 1200 + allocGas(len)
verdicts.tldr: the flat gas price assumes nothing scales with input, but the returned type name is built at the length of the declared name, so long names run under-charged
verdicts.details: native_gas.go:157 prices objectInfo at Base 1200, SizeFlat, with the comment 'nothing here scales with caller input'. declaredTypeName returns `dt.PkgPath + "." + string(dt.Name)`, an allocation and copy proportional to the identifier length, which the flat row does not bill. The finder measured 827 us at a 1 MB name against roughly 196k gas charged; it only matters at extreme identifier lengths. Fix: charge a SizeReturnLen post-slope on the type-name result, or correct the gas comment.

verdicts.details: creatingRealmPath returns rlm.Path for any record GetRealmByID finds, and GetRealmByID (store.go:495-503) resolves any package path through pkgPathFromPkgID and GetPackageRealm with no realm-path check. A stdlib func value is therefore Of-ok, with PkgPath documented as 'the realm that created the object' (reflect.gno:61) naming a stdlib. verdicts.verify_by: grep every SetNewTime/SetObjectID site in gnovm/pkg/gnolang for one that stamps NewTime with a zero PkgID
verdicts.tldr: the godoc says IsFinalized is enough to avoid the panic, but the guard also panics on a zero PkgID; that case cannot happen today
verdicts.details: DeriveObjectCryptoAddr panics on `!oid.IsFinalized() || oid.PkgID.IsZero()`, and its godoc tells callers to check IsFinalized, which is only `NewTime != 0`. The only NewTime stamps outside unmarshal are realm.go:2031 and :2041 inside assignNewObjectID, after the zero-PkgID fix-up at :1995-2003. So X_objectInfo never hits the second half, and the only cost is godoc advice that covers half the guard. Fix: say in the godoc that both halves must be set, or have X_objectInfo check PkgID.IsZero too.

verdicts.verify_by: grep -n 'chain/reflect' -A22 gnovm/stdlibs/generated.go | grep p0 ; expect gno.X("any"), not gno.AnyT()
verdicts.tldr: the ADR says the binding maps any to gno.AnyT(), but the generated binding is gno.X("any")
verdicts.details: GnoTypeExpression returns gno.AnyT() only when the type expression renders as "interface{}" (misc/genstd/mapping.go:39-41), and the Gno-side `any` renders as "any", so generated.go:1210 carries `Type: gno.X("any")`. The ADR's Consequences bullet names code that does not exist. Fix: change the ADR to gno.X("any").
